heroes: A Michigan mineral review should connect the county legal description, ownership fraction, producing or undeveloped status, paid decimal, Antrim decline evidence, written terms, and recording plan.
Read the Well Before Comparing the Offer
Antrim gas can decline quickly and then settle into a long production tail. Several statement months and the actual paid decimal matter more than a flat mailbox number.
Untangle the Farm Conveyance and Heir Fraction
Old deeds, probate records, reservations, leases, and division orders should describe the same Michigan tract before a partial or full interest is priced.
A royalty statement proves current paid production. Leases, permits, and nearby wells can add context without becoming guaranteed future income.

locations: A Michigan location page should lead back to a real tract record. The working file identifies the county, township, range, section, legal description, acreage, mineral reservation, estate type, ownership fraction, and the deed, probate file, or trust instrument that supports the present ownership claim.
Connect Local Production to the Actual Interest

Antrim, Niagaran, Dundee, Trenton-Black River, and other Michigan production evidence varies by county and formation. Operator names, well records, unit boundaries, statement months, paid decimals, downtime, and recent volumes should be checked for the documented interest instead of assumed from a nearby place name.
Keep the Local Review in Writing

The owner copy for {name} should retain the source deed, legal description, ownership reconstruction, statement evidence, written offer assumptions, retained-rights language, settlement record, and recording reference. That sequence lets the location guide support a transaction without pretending every parcel in the area has the same production or value.
investing: Locate {name} on the Michigan Owner Record

A Michigan mineral investment should be traced from the recorded interest to the paid decimal before a yield or multiple is trusted. The file identifies the county, legal description, estate type, ownership fraction, lease royalty, unit participation, products, deductions, taxes, producing wells, operator, statement months, and title assumptions still open.

Antrim biogenic-gas wells can move from dewatering and early production into a mature, long decline tail. Several statement months, historical volumes, downtime, realized pricing, and the present operator should support the base case rather than one unusually large or small check.

A current royalty statement is direct cash-flow evidence. Nearby leases, permits, units, wells, and operator activity can add context for undeveloped acreage without becoming guaranteed drilling, future reserves, or a promised royalty stream.

{name} still depends on the estate described in the recorded Michigan chain. The investment file should identify the legal description, acquired fraction, reservations, depth or formation limits, present payor, suspense status, and unresolved probate, trust, or heirship issue.
Stress the Paid Decimal Against Actual Statements

The review should compare several statement months rather than treating one check as normal. Gas, oil, and natural-gas-liquids volumes, price, taxes, deductions, prior-period adjustments, downtime, and suspense releases can move independently and change the apparent cash yield.
Write the Downside Case Before the Upside Case

A disciplined Michigan mineral model tests lower volumes, weaker realized pricing, longer downtime, higher title expense, operator concentration, delayed development, and limited resale liquidity before giving weight to upside activity. The downside case should identify which assumption changes the value conclusion first.
Set a Review Date for Every Material Assumption

Production, operator activity, unit records, statement deductions, title status, and market liquidity can change on different schedules. The owner ledger assigns a source date and a future review date to each material assumption so the investment case can be updated from records instead of memory.
Reconcile the Investment Memo to the Recorded Asset

Before a Michigan mineral package is approved, the investment memo, acquisition agreement, deed, legal description, acquired fraction, retained rights, title exceptions, funding record, and post-closing owner copy should describe the same asset. Any difference is resolved in writing before the yield case is treated as final.
exchange-1031: Potential exchange treatment should be discussed with a qualified intermediary and independent tax counsel before a Michigan mineral sale closes or proceeds are received. The file identifies the selling owner or entity, property description, expected proceeds, target closing date, statutory deadlines, and proposed replacement property.
Keep Michigan Curative Work and Federal Timing Distinct

Deed work, probate, heirship, trusts, corrective instruments, payor records, and county recording can move on a different schedule from exchange deadlines. Each open item needs a responsible professional, a dated status, and a written effect on closing.

The sale agreement, deed, legal description, retained-rights language, settlement statement, intermediary instructions, and replacement identification should not quietly change the acreage, estate, formation, depth, county, owner fraction, or entity that appears elsewhere in the file.
Tie the Exchange File to the Michigan Interest

{name} should not float free of the tract record. The owner file should show the exact county, legal description, estate type, ownership fraction, retained rights, deed form, settlement amount, and recording reference beside the intermediary timeline.

The qualified intermediary handles exchange funds and required notices; independent tax counsel evaluates eligibility and reporting; title counsel addresses deed, entity, probate, trust, and curative questions; the closing team confirms the tract, estate, fraction, consideration, and Michigan recording package.
Reconcile Identification Language to the Replacement Record

A replacement-property identification should be reviewed against the records available at the time. Names, legal descriptions, county references, entity ownership, percentage interests, and stated alternatives need consistent language across the notice, purchase documents, title file, and closing instructions.
Archive the Completed Exchange and Owner Files Together

The final owner copy should retain intermediary instructions, dated identification notices, settlement statements, recorded conveyances, title correspondence, funding records, replacement-property documents, professional advice, and the Michigan mineral ledger. Keeping both records together makes later reporting and ownership questions easier to answer.
Close the Calendar With a Document Inventory

After closing, the dated exchange calendar should be reconciled to the final settlement statement, intermediary account record, identification notice, replacement closing package, recorded Michigan conveyance, professional advice, and tax-reporting file. Missing documents are listed with an owner and follow-up date rather than assumed complete.
